hints: Notice you are given Young modulus $E = 2.0 \times 10^{11}$ $\text{Pa}$, length $L = 1.6$ $\text{m}$ and diameter $0.48 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{m}$, and asked for spring constant $k = F/x$ in $\text{N m}^{-1}$.
Recall $E = (F/A)/(x/L)$, so rearrange to $F/x = EA/L$ - you first need the cross-sectional area $A$ from the diameter.
Remember radius is half the $0.48 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{m}$ diameter and $A = \pi r^2$, then check that $EA/L$ has units of $\text{N m}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Write the Young modulus in terms of force $F$ and extension $x$: $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} = (F/A)/(x/L) = FL/(Ax)$. Rearrange for spring constant $k = F/x = EA/L$.
Calculate the radius: $r = d/2 = 0.48 \times 10^{-3}/2 = 0.24 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{m}$. Then area $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \times (0.24 \times 10^{-3})^2 \approx 1.81 \times 10^{-7}$ $\text{m}^2$.

Evaluate numerator: $2.0 \times 10^{11} \times 1.81 \times 10^{-7} \approx 3.62 \times 10^4$ $\text{N}$, then divide by $1.6$ to get $k \approx 2.26 \times 10^4$ $\text{N m}^{-1}$, about $2.3 \times 10^4$ $\text{N m}^{-1}$.
